Stated Claim / Post Context:
Elgin News Digest: Three Elgin-area people honored by state treasurer; Elgin funeral home rebrands, adds Cary location

Roundup of small news items for the Elgin area.

Actual Article Body:
eNewspaper

Sign up for email newsletters

Sign up for email newsletters

eNewspaper

Trending:

Three people with ties to Elgin were among the nine community leaders honored Thursday, Sept. 24, by Illinois State Treasurer Michael Frerichs at a Hispanic Heritage Month celebration in Chicago.

Elisa Lara, clinical coordinator at VNA Health Care in Elgin, received the award for Outstanding Commitment to Community Service, according to a news release.

Christina Gonzalez and her brother Larry Gonzalez were recognized with the Outstanding Service in Business award. The siblings co-own Los Comales, which has 18 restaurant locations throughout the Chicago area, including one in Elgin.

Frerichs told those at the celebration that they gathered to show their respect and appreciation for Hispanic and Latino neighbors whose contributions are making communities better places to live, work and raise families, according to the news release.

Elgin Community College will host an electric vehicle technology open house from 4 to 6 p.m. Wednesday, Oct. 14, at the Manufacturing and Technology Center, Building S, Room 111, 1600 Spartan Drive.

The open house will feature interactive demonstrations, an outdoor EV showcase and a chance to learn from ECC faculty about high-voltage battery systems, EV charging infrastructure, renewable energy and career opportunities.

To register to attend the free event, go to elgin.edu/about/campus-visitor-information/mtc/ev-tech-open-house.

State Rep. Anna Moeller, D-Elgin, will host her annual Youth and Family Resource Fair from 5 to 6:30 p.m. Tuesday, Oct. 13, at the Gail Borden Public Library, 270 N. Grove Ave., Elgin.

Two dozen vendors are expected to be at the free event to provide information on volunteer opportunities, after-school programs, health and wellness resources, and career readiness tools, a news release said. Light refreshments will be served.

“I look forward to our Youth and Family Resource Fair each year because it gives us the chance to invest in our young people and connect families with resources and make a meaningful difference in their lives,” Moeller said in the release.

For more information, call 847-841-7130.

Symonds-Madison Funeral Home in Elgin is now known as Symonds Family Chapels and has added a location in Cary.

“While our name and look are changing, Daniel and Joy Symonds and the team you know remain here, continuing to provide the same personal and compassionate care,” a social media post about the rebranding said.

The Elgin chapel, located at 305 Park St., was founded in downtown Elgin in 1921 and, according to the business’s website, has undergone several incarnations over the decades. Daniel Symonds, a second-generation funeral director, and his wife, Joy, bought what was the Madison Funeral Home in 2013.

The Symonds Family Chapel in Cary was formerly known as the Kahle-Moore Funeral Home, 403 Silver Lake Road, according to the website. It was built in 1964 by James Kahle and purchased by Steven Moore in 1978.

Elgin resident Rick Poulton will serve as the 2026-27 president of the Kiwanis Children’s Fund.

Poulton previously served as president-elect and vice president of the fund after becoming a trustee in 2022, according to a news release. He is a member of the Kiwanis clubs of Elgin and Geneva and has served the Kiwanis Illinois-Eastern Iowa District as a lieutenant governor and governor.

His volunteer work includes 10 years as a court-appointed special advocate for children in Kane County, participating in a Reading Buddy preschool program, and working with Food for Greater Elgin and with Senior Services of Elgin. Poulton also is a member of the housing board for the Association for Individual Development.

Prior to retirement, he was a marketing director for AT&T.

Two stolen Renoir paintings found, six people arrested

Two Renoir paintings stolen from a museum in southern France last month have been found, and six people arrested, local authorities said.

Actual Article Body:
Emergency

Backstory

Newsletters

中文新闻

BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

TOK PISIN

Topic:Law, Crime and Justice

Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano by Renoir was stolen in September. (Wikimedia Commons: Pierre-Auguste Renoir)

Two Renoir paintings stolen from a museum in southern France last month have been found, and six people arrested, local authorities said on Friday.

The mayor of Cagnes-sur-Mer, the town that hosts the Renoir Museum, Bryan Masson, issued a statement praising investigators who tracked down the paintings and suspects.

"These two paintings are not simply works of art. They are part of our city's history, our heritage," Mr Masson said.

Mayor Bryan Masson addressed the press outside Musée Renoir after the heist. (AFP: Valery Hache)

The statement did not elaborate on how the paintings were tracked down.

The two missing paintings were Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano and Young Woman at the Well.

Police officers patrolled the front entrance of the Musée Renoir after the early-morning heist. (AFP: Valery Hache)

The thieves sliced through a fence, climbed through a window and initially stole four valuable Renoir paintings in the heist last month, but abandoned two of the artworks as they fled, authorities said.

Thieves sliced through a fence, grabbed 9 million euros worth of art, dumped half of them in a garden and escaped in under three minutes.

The whole operation took less than 3 minutes and targeted the most valuable works in the Renoir Museum in the town of Cagnes-sur-Mer, the regional prosecutor’s office said.

Investigators launched a national search for the perpetrators.

The theft conjured up painful memories of the spectacular heist of crown jewels at the Louvre Museum in Paris last year and revived calls for better security and better funding for the many cultural sites large and small that dot France’s landscape.
